---
title: "04 — Multi-DoF suspension (full campaign)"
---

A 3-DoF suspension (POS / PIT / YAW) run through the real `TwinBackend` and
`SysIDLoop` — the same code path the CLI executes.  This is the reference
example for a full **Pintelon-Schoukens** campaign: every DoF is driven by a
*periodic* multisine, the response is turned into a **leakage-free** reference-based
FRF, and each accumulated FRF is fit by the Gaussian **maximum-likelihood**
estimator (`gml`).

The campaign exercises every component end to end:

- the Pintelon-Schoukens optimal-excitation designer for each DoF sequentially
- the periodic-multisine, leakage-free FRF measurement (no windowing, no leakage)
- maximum-likelihood (`gml`) parametric fits with inverse-variance accumulation across passes
- the fractional-uncertainty stop criterion
- Plotly-rendered convergence and Bode plots

```{python}
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

from system_ident.config import RunConfig
from system_ident.loop import SysIDLoop
from system_ident.excitation import multisine_from_psd
from system_ident.design.pintelon import optimal_excitation

cfg = {
    "run": {"name": "susp3dof", "excitation_mode": "sequential"},
    "channels": {
        "excitation": {"POS": "C1:EXC_POS", "PIT": "C1:EXC_PIT", "YAW": "C1:EXC_YAW"},
        "readback":   {"POS": "C1:RSP_POS", "PIT": "C1:RSP_PIT", "YAW": "C1:RSP_YAW"},
    },
    "measurement": {
        "fs": 32, "freq_min": 0.1, "freq_max": 5.0,
        "segment_duration": 64.0, "n_segments": 4, "px_total": 1.0,
    },
    "strategy": {
        "estimator": "gml",
        "input_designer": "pintelon_schoukens",
        "n_design_iter": 3,
    },
    "twin": {
        "sensor_asd": 1e-9,
        "plant": {
            "POS": {"resonances": [[0.6, 20], [1.5, 30]], "gain": 300},
            "PIT": {"resonances": [[0.8, 15], [2.2, 25]], "gain": 120},
            "YAW": {"resonances": [[1.2, 18]],            "gain": 80},
        },
    },
    "priors": {
        "POS": {"resonances": [[0.55, 18], [1.6, 28]], "gain": 250},
        "PIT": {"resonances": [[0.75, 13], [2.3, 22]], "gain": 150},
        "YAW": {"resonances": [[1.1, 16]],             "gain": 100},
    },
    "safety": {
        "actuator_sat": 1000.0,
        "rms_ceiling": {"POS": 1000.0, "PIT": 1000.0, "YAW": 1000.0},
        "ramp_down_secs": 2.0,
    },
    "stop_criteria": {"uncertainty_target": 0.05, "max_iter": 2},
}

rc       = RunConfig(raw=cfg)
backend  = rc.build_twin_backend(seed=0)
priors   = rc.build_priors()
watchdog = rc.build_watchdog(backend)
loop     = SysIDLoop(backend, rc.build_estimator(), rc.build_designer(), watchdog)
```

## Is the excitation safe? — the measurement time series

Before trusting any campaign result, look at the **raw time series** of one
injection.  Here we reproduce exactly what the loop does for a single DoF (POS):
design the Pintelon-Schoukens optimal *periodic* multisine, inject it, and read
back the drive monitor and the mirror response.  The drive is a smooth, bounded,
low-crest Schroeder waveform — the suspension is being *coaxed*, not slammed —
and its peak sits far inside the `actuator_sat = 1000` limit.

```{python}
#| label: fig-suspension-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "One POS injection, first ~60 s. The drive (top) is a smooth, low-crest periodic multisine; the mirror response (bottom) is a bounded steady oscillation. The peak drive stays well inside the actuator-saturation limit, so the optimal excitation is safe to run on the real suspension."

SKY, GOLD, GREEN = '#1F8AC0', '#C8973A', '#2D9D6B'

m         = cfg["measurement"]
fs        = float(m["fs"])
nperseg   = int(m["segment_duration"] * fs)
n_periods = int(m["n_segments"])
px_total  = float(m["px_total"])
dur       = nperseg * n_periods / fs

f_all   = np.fft.rfftfreq(nperseg, 1 / fs)
band    = (f_all >= m["freq_min"]) & (f_all <= m["freq_max"])
freq_ms = f_all[band]

exc_ch = cfg["channels"]["excitation"]["POS"]
rb_ch  = cfg["channels"]["readback"]["POS"]

# Quiet readback PSD -> design weighting (the same Pyy the loop uses), then the
# Pintelon-Schoukens optimal drive PSD and its periodic-multisine realisation.
Pyy   = SysIDLoop._noise_psd(backend.read([rb_ch], dur)[rb_ch], fs, nperseg, band)
Pxx   = optimal_excitation(freq_ms, priors["POS"], Pyy, px_total, n_iter=3)
drive = multisine_from_psd(Pxx, fs, nperseg, n_periods, freq_ms, seed=0)

backend.inject(exc_ch, drive, fs)
seg = backend.read([exc_ch, rb_ch], dur)
backend.inject(exc_ch, np.zeros_like(drive), fs)   # clear the demo drive for a clean campaign

t = np.arange(int(60 * fs)) / fs
fig0 = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.10,
    subplot_titles=['<b>Drive</b> — POS actuator (Pintelon-Schoukens multisine)',
                    '<b>Mirror motion</b> — POS response'],
)
fig0.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=seg[exc_ch][:t.size], mode='lines',
               line=dict(color=SKY, width=1.3), name='drive (POS)'), row=1, col=1)
fig0.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=seg[rb_ch][:t.size], mode='lines',
               line=dict(color=GOLD, width=1.5), name='POS motion'), row=2, col=1)
fig0.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=460,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=50, b=50),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.05, xanchor='right', x=1),
)
fig0.update_yaxes(title_text='drive [cts]', row=1, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig0.update_yaxes(title_text='motion [a.u.]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig0.update_xaxes(title_text='time [s]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig0.show()
```

## Run the campaign

```{python}
result = loop.run(rc.raw, priors, seed=0)

print(f"Campaign done: {result.done}")
for dof, model in result.models.items():
    print(f"  {dof}  den: {np.round(model.den, 3)}")
```

## Convergence — fractional uncertainty per DoF

```{python}
#| label: fig-convergence
#| fig-cap: "Fractional parameter uncertainty (worst parameter per DoF) vs campaign iteration. Each DoF is excited sequentially; the uncertainty drops as optimal passes accumulate. Use the legend to toggle individual DoFs."

colors = {'POS': SKY, 'PIT': GOLD, 'YAW': GREEN}
symbols = {'POS': 'circle', 'PIT': 'square', 'YAW': 'diamond'}

fig = go.Figure()

for dof in result.models:
    pts = [(r.iteration, r.max_frac_uncertainty)
           for r in result.history if r.dof == dof]
    if not pts:
        continue
    it, frac = zip(*pts)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=list(it), y=list(frac),
        mode='lines+markers',
        line=dict(color=colors[dof], width=2.2),
        marker=dict(symbol=symbols[dof], size=9,
                    color=colors[dof], line=dict(color='white', width=1.5)),
        name=dof,
        hovertemplate=f'<b>{dof}</b><br>Iteration %{{x}}<br>σ/θ = %{{y:.3e}}<extra></extra>',
    ))

# Target line
target = cfg["stop_criteria"]["uncertainty_target"]
fig.add_hline(
    y=target, line_dash='dot', line_color='rgba(100,120,160,0.5)',
    annotation_text=f'  target = {target}', annotation_position='right',
    annotation_font=dict(size=11, color='rgba(100,120,160,0.85)', family='Outfit, sans-serif'),
)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=380,
    margin=dict(l=65, r=20, t=20, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1),
    xaxis=dict(title='Iteration', dtick=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
    yaxis=dict(title='Max fractional uncertainty', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
)
fig.show()
```

## Recovered vs true transfer functions

```{python}
#| label: fig-bode-all
#| fig-cap: "Recovered (dashed) vs true (solid) plant for all three DoFs. Click a trace in the legend to isolate a single DoF."

freq = np.linspace(0.1, 5.0, 600)

fig2 = go.Figure()

colors_true = {'POS': SKY,  'PIT': GOLD,  'YAW': GREEN}
colors_fit  = {'POS': '#63BBE0', 'PIT': '#E5C67A', 'YAW': '#6DC99B'}

for dof in result.models:
    true_model      = backend.plant[dof]
    recovered_model = result.models[dof]

    fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=freq, y=np.abs(true_model.eval(freq)),
        mode='lines', line=dict(color=colors_true[dof], width=2.5),
        name=f'{dof} — true',
        hovertemplate=f'<b>{dof} true</b><br>%{{x:.3f}} Hz   |G| = %{{y:.4f}}<extra></extra>',
    ))
    fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=freq, y=np.abs(recovered_model.eval(freq)),
        mode='lines', line=dict(color=colors_fit[dof], width=2.0, dash='dash'),
        name=f'{dof} — recovered',
        hovertemplate=f'<b>{dof} recovered</b><br>%{{x:.3f}} Hz   |G| = %{{y:.4f}}<extra></extra>',
    ))

fig2.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=400,
    margin=dict(l=65, r=20, t=20, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(
        orientation='v', yanchor='top', y=1, xanchor='left', x=1.02,
        bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1,
        font=dict(size=10),
    ),
    xaxis=dict(title='Frequency  [Hz]', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
    yaxis=dict(title='|G(f)|', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
)
fig2.show()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Sequential vs simultaneous excitation

The config sets `excitation_mode: sequential` — one DoF is driven at a time,
which keeps the response measurement unambiguous (no cross-coupling between
excitation channels in the periodic FRF estimate).  A future `simultaneous` mode
would require careful coherence-based channel separation.
:::
